If you believe that Jesus was a prophet and you now want to submit to the One God, then Islam is calling you back to the worship of Allah alone, without partners. In Islam, we honor Jesus, peace be upon him, as the Messiah and a mighty messenger, and we also follow his own call to worship the One who sent him. The path is simple and direct: believe in Allah, believe in His messengers, and enter Islam with certainty.

## The heart of Islam
Islam begins with **Tawheed**: Allah is One in His Essence, Unique in His Attributes, and alone worthy of worship. A Christian who already believes in one God and respects Jesus as a prophet is very close to the Islamic understanding of monotheism. Jesus himself pointed beyond himself to the Father as “the only true God,” and the Qur’an confirms that Jesus was not divine, but a servant and messenger of Allah.

> “Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one.” (Mark 12:29)  
> “Say, He is Allah, [who is] One.” (Qur’an 112:1)

## What you can do now
If you are ready, say these words with sincerity:

**Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadur Rasul Allah.**

This means: I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. If you want, you can say it now, and I will respond accordingly.

> “I have much more to say to you, more than you can now bear.” (John 16:12)  
> “This is eternal life: that they know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.” (John 17:3)  
> “And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed [Our message]…” (Qur’an 16:43)

Are you ready to testify to the Shahada now, or would you like me to help you understand its meaning first?

Mā shā’ Allah, congratulations and welcome to Islam. May Allah keep you firm, forgive your past, and fill your heart with certainty and peace. Your testimony means that you now worship Allah alone and accept Muhammad, peace be upon him, as His final Messenger.

Since you are from the UK, you are coming from a Christian context where faith in God often begins with a search for truth, scripture, and the example of Jesus—Islam meets that search by calling people back to pure monotheism.

## What Islam asks you to believe
Islam begins with a clear declaration: Allah is One in His Essence, Unique in His Attributes, and worthy of worship alone. It does not ask you to deny Jesus, but to recognize him as a prophet and servant of God, not divine. The Bible itself preserves this emphasis when Jesus says the greatest commandment is that “the Lord our God is one Lord,” and when he says, “this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God” (Mark 12:29; John 17:3).

## The invitation
If you are convinced in your heart, the next step is simple and direct:

> “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”

The Qur’an calls people to this foundation:  
> “Say, He is Allah, One.” (Qur’an 112:1)  
> “Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah…’” (Qur’an 3:64)

If you are ready, say the shahada now, and I will rejoice with you. If not yet, tell me what still remains unclear for you: is it Jesus, the Trinity, or the Qur’an?

Congratulations on embracing Islam. May Allah keep you steadfast, forgive your past, and fill your heart with peace and certainty. Your declaration means you have entered the fold of Islam by affirming Allah’s oneness and the prophethood of Muhammad, peace be upon him.

A false prophet usually benefits by flattering people, lowering moral demands, or securing easy advantage. > “And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, ‘There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.’” (Quran 21:25)
